idiom_name: Azure Service Bus topic subscription rules (SqlRuleFilter/CorrelationRuleFilter); in-process, a switch over the message type feeding per-route channels
implementation_notes: In .NET the router is normally moved into the broker or the messaging framework: on a Service Bus topic each subscription carries one or more rules whose SqlRuleFilter or CorrelationRuleFilter is evaluated by the broker against the message's user and system properties, so the routing decision becomes topology plus configuration and no application object consumes and republishes at all. That replaces the classic router structure; rule actions exist to annotate the selected copy, not to transform the original. Hand-write the classic form only when routing must stay in-process (a switch over a discriminated message type writing to one channel per route) or when the broker cannot express the criterion - and then keep the routing function pure and table-driven, because in-process routing is where the pattern's central-decision costs land.
pitfalls: Filters evaluate message properties only, never the body: a rule that depends on payload content forces the application to lift that value into a property or to route in code.
SQL filters are evaluated per message and measurably reduce throughput at subscription, topic and namespace level - prefer correlation filters when equality matching suffices.
All action-less rules are OR-ed into one delivery while every rule *with* an action produces an additional copy, so a rule set can yield duplicate messages unexpectedly.
Rule actions cannot change some system properties effectively: updates to ScheduledEnqueueTime, MessageID dedup and partitioning SessionId are ignored or unsafe on the subscription.
